triggers: a kernel on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942) risks the '49. BLOCK_M=64 regresses occupancy 3→2 on MI308X flash attention' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942): 49. BLOCK_M=64 regresses occupancy 3→2 on MI308X flash attention

problem.statement: Pitfalls: FlyDSL Flash Attention on MI308X (gfx942) -- 49. BLOCK_M=64 regresses occupancy 3→2 on MI308X flash attention

payload.attempted: With BLOCK_M=128 at occupancy 3, try BLOCK_M=64 for better tail handling (S=316 with BLOCK_M=64 gives 5 Q tiles instead of 3, better CU utilization). Smaller tiles should also reduce register pressure.
payload.lesson: On CDNA3 with MFMA32, BLOCK_M=128 (4 waves, 256 threads) is the sweet spot for flash attention. BLOCK_M=64 only makes sense if the VGPR footprint can be kept under 256/thread (occupancy 2 with 2 waves needs 256 VGPRs/wave from 512 total).

established_fact.mechanism: BLOCK_M=64 uses 128 threads (2 waves × 64 threads) instead of 256 threads (4 waves × 64 threads). With only 2 waves and head_dim=64, each thread must hold more Q and accumulator state, pushing VGPRs above the 128 limit. At 2 waves/SIMD, each KV iteration has half the compute throughput but the same fixed overhead (LDS loads, mask loads, barriers).

payload.observed: 50.2 TFLOPS (from 64.9). Occupancy dropped from 3 to 2 waves/SIMD. KV iterations doubled (10 iterations for S=320 with BLOCK_M=64 vs 5 with BLOCK_M=128).
